wall.text: Coding agents are fast. In minutes, they read your code, change ten files, and explain it all...

statement.text: But humans see faster than they read.

canvas.text: Mirador gives your agent a canvas.

show.text: So instead of describing, it shows you. Flows, architecture, mockups and charts, drawn right beside the conversation.

ask.text: When a decision is yours, it asks with pictures. Click an option, and it carries on.

review.text: Reviews become a guided tour of the change, in the order the code runs, with findings pinned to the lines they're about.

reviewAsk.text: Question a finding, and the agent answers and rewrites it in place.

reviewPost.text: Keep the ones you agree with, and post them to the pull request.

overview.text: Run your agents across all your projects. See who's working, who's done, and who needs you.

edit.text: Approve every edit with its diff.

changes.text: Every change since your last commit, even outside the project.

terminals.text: Your terminals sit right beside the conversation.

point.text: Point at anything it drew, and ask about it, or have it changed.

plugins.text: Mirador grows with plugins. Your agent knows the official ones, and installs one when you say so.

media.text: Like Media. Mark what's wrong on the frame, and the agent cuts the video and renders it.

voiceAsk.text: How long will the switch-over take, and what could go wrong?

voiceReply.text: About ten minutes, read-only. It waits for replication to catch up before it switches.

end.text: See what your coding agent means.
